subject: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Olivia / team — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and proposed next steps for the POC environment selection so we can align on scope: 

Summary of needs you shared:
- Evaluating LLM-powered product search & personalized recommendations across checkout flows
- Sensitive PII in a subset of logs; security/compliance constraints noted
- Success criteria: generation relevance (top-3 CTR lift), p95 latency < 300ms, cost target <= $X per 1M tokens, and stable throughput of ~200 qps for peak windows

POC options we proposed on the call (trade-offs):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood hosted API with isolated API key and workload tagging. Pros: same-day onboarding, minimal infra work, good for quality + latency baseline. Cons: data residency / policy review required for some logs.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved environment): short-term reserved capacity on a dedicated GPU pool. Pros: predictable throughput, easier to simulate load. Cons: lead time ~2–3 weeks.
3) VPC trial (private deployment): Private control plane + customer VPC peering (best for sensitive data). Pros: meets strict data controls. Cons: setup time 3–6 weeks depending on networking approvals.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Short (2-week) hosted trial to validate prompt sets, relevance, and rough latency/cost.
- In parallel, kick off security/IT for a VPC trial approval path and scoped Dedicated sandbox if VPC not feasible.

Requested from your side to start hosted trial:
- A short representative dataset (sample log + product catalog) or links to S3 sample (we can use synthetic subset)
- IP ranges and egress rules if you want to lock requests (we can also provide allowlist IPs)
- Point of contact for procurement & security (copying Jordan for enablement)

I’ll attach a short POC outline and proposed success criteria + timeline. If that sounds good, we can schedule a 30-min kickoff with Dev to get keys and run first tests.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: POC-outline.pdf

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonretail.com
Date: 2026-02-28T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few quick notes from my side: 

- Our security team will likely prefer VPC given the sensitive order/customer IDs that could appear in logs. That said, we’re open to a short hosted trial if we can avoid sending full PII to a hosted endpoint (masking or truncated logs).
- Timeline: procurement needs a ballpark cost for a 2-week dedicated sandbox and an estimate for the VPC onboarding (network & security).
- Key success criteria we care most about: top-3 relevance improvement vs current ranking, p95 latency under 300ms for 99% traffic, and clear logging/audit capability for requests.

CC’ing procurement to weigh in on cost & temporary contracts. I’ll also loop in our infra lead separately for network details.

Olivia Chen
Senior Product Manager — Search & Personalization
Horizon Retail
olivia.chen@horizonretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Olivia — thanks, that’s helpful. Below is a more concrete POC plan (attached) and an evaluation matrix so you can share with security/procurement.

POC duration & phases:
- Phase 0 (prep, 3 days): sample dataset ingestion, API keys, allowlist IPs, and test harness setup.
- Phase 1 (hosted trial, 2 weeks): run canonical prompt set, measure relevance metrics, latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, and cost run-rate.
- Phase 2 (dedicated sandbox or VPC, optional, 2–4 weeks): repeat same tests at scale and validate stability under load.

Success criteria (examples we’ll measure):
- Relevance: +8% top-3 CTR (vs baseline) on the evaluation prompt set
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for targeted request mix
- Throughput: sustain 200 qps for 10-minute windows with <1% error rate
- Cost: projected unit cost <= $X per 1M tokens (we’ll produce cost runbook)
- Observability: request-level tracing + audit logs retained for 30 days (scoped per agreement)

Ownership:
- Redwood: onboarding, API keys, model selection recommendations, initial eval harness
- Horizon: provide sample dataset (or S3 access), security contact, procurement approval
- Dev enablement: Dev Patel to run environment setup and load tests

Immediate next steps:
1) Horizon: send sample dataset or a synthetic extract + IP allowlist (if you’ll be using allowlist).
2) Redwood: schedule 30-min kickoff with Dev and hand off POC-outline.pdf.

Forwarding network checklist to Dev for technical details.

Thanks — attaching POC-outline.pdf for your security and procurement review.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: POC-outline.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Olivia — quick technical checklist and clarifications for the VPC / dedicated options: 

If you want to proceed with VPC trial: 
- We’ll need a CIDR range for the peered subnet and a contact for VPN/peering provisioning.
- Suggested firewall rules: allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood control plane on 443 and our NAT IPs (we provide).
- For shorter hosted trial: we can provide allowlist IPs + short-term masking patterns to remove PII from logs.

Test artifacts we recommend you prepare:
- 1k sample queries (production-like distribution) + expected relevance labels (CSV)
- A small synthetic dataset (S3 link) with ~50k product records for cold-start tests
- If you want load tests: list of expected QPS and time windows (dev can simulate)

I’m attaching a short network-checklist.xlsx with the exact fields we’ll need from your infra team. Typical timeline for VPC peering once tickets are opened is ~2–3 weeks, depending on change window approvals. Dedicated sandbox provisioning is ~10 business days.

Let me know a few 30-min windows for a technical kickoff next week and I’ll block time.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: network-checklist.xlsx

From: procurement@horizonretail.com <procurement@horizonretail.com>

Date: 2026-03-03T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Marissa / Olivia —

We can evaluate a temporary dedicated sandbox; please provide a commercial estimate for a 2-week reserved environment (GPU instance sizing, expected throughput, and any one-time setup fees). Also provide a SOC2 / security pack and the DocuSign for a temporary one-off SOW so we can fast-track procurement.

If VPC is required, we’ll need a statement of work and estimated engineering hours for onboarding. Thanks.

— Horizon Procurement
procurement@horizonretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@horizonretail.com>, procurement@horizonretail.com
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment selection: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Thanks everyone — quick sync & decision proposal so we can move forward without blocking: 

Decision recommendation (based on risk/time-to-value):
- Start with a 2-week hosted trial (non-production keys, data masking options enabled) to validate quality and measure p50/p95 latency and cost. This will give Horizon fast signal on relevance and allow us to iterate on prompts and eval sets.
- Parallel track: begin the security intake for VPC trial and get the network checklist completed. If security signs off within 2 weeks, we will provision a VPC trial; otherwise, we’ll escalate to a Dedicated sandbox for the scale tests.

Deliverables & owners:
- Hosted trial onboarding (Marissa / Dev): create API keys, provide sample prompt harness, and run initial 1k eval queries — due 2026-03-09
- Procurement estimate & SOW (Marissa): send 2-week dedicated sandbox pricing + DocuSign template — due 2026-03-06
- Security intake (Olivia): share network contact and indicate any mandatory controls for logs — due 2026-03-06

Kickoff: I’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff for 2026-03-05 at 11:00 PT unless anyone needs a different time. Link: https://app.redwood.inference/sessions/kickoff-12345

If this plan looks good, please reply-all with approval and we’ll begin.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
